land.text: the Ili Valley and the Issyk-Kul basin: 'the Wusun drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled the area'; the royal court Chigu 'in a side valley leading to Issyk Kul'

predecessors.note: The Yuezhi held the Ili from about 165 BC (yuezhi dossier). The Wusun themselves had lived 'between the Qilian Mountains and Dunhuang (Gansu)' until the Yuezhi and Xiongnu struck them (Wusun page); that Hexi homeland is not drawn.

capitals.name: Chigu (Red Valley City), near Issyk-Kul
capitals.note: 'The Royal Court of the Wusun, the walled city of Chigu, was located in a side valley leading to Issyk Kul ... its exact location has not been established'; the coordinates are a point on the southern shore, approximate. The page dates no change of capital. Latitude moved from 42.4 (a point inside the lake on the grid) to 42.15, on the southern shore as intended (reviewer ia-01-b, 2026-10-18).

correction.text: no Wusun state on the Ili in -170..-133; the same shape holds for -132..-67 (wusun_-132)

keyframe_review.note: -170..-145 puts the Wusun on the Ili 37 years before they took it: they 'originally lived between the Qilian Mountains and Dunhuang (Gansu)', their king Nandoumi was killed by the Yuezhi around 173 BC and 'In 133-132 BC, the Wusun drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled the area' (the Yuezhi dossier holds the Ili from 165). The shape itself is the Wusun's Ili shape; it belongs to -132..-67, where Cliopatria has no Wusun shape at all (see wusun_-132). Nothing is drawn for the Wusun in -170..-133.

correction.text: the Ili Valley and the Issyk-Kul basin: 'the Wusun drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled the area'; the royal court Chigu 'in a side valley leading to Issyk Kul'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -132..-67, filling Cliopatria's gap (its Wusun shapes stop at -145 and resume at -66): the Ili and Issyk-Kul after 133-132 BC, the Wusun's rise under Liejiaomi, the war with the Xiongnu around 80 BC and the joint campaign of 72 BC. The -66 shape (205,697 km2) is used unchanged.

205,697 km2, the Ili and Issyk-Kul. 'The Wusun subsequently took over the Ili Valley, expanding over a large area'; Zhang Qian counted 630,000 people, 120,000 families and 188,000 archers. Neighbours: 'To their north-west the Wusun bordered Kangju', Dayuan to the west and the Tarim city states to the south. The page has no area figure to compare.

194,516 km2. 'During the peak of the protectorate's power in 51 BCE, the Wusun nation was brought under Han submission': the Wusun are a Han tributary from then (the vassal tint belongs to the han-dynasty dossier). The page does not say whether the Wusun lay inside the protectorate.
194,432 km2, 6-13. 'In 5 BC ... the Wusun attempted to raid Yueban pastures' and in 2 BC a chieftain took 80,000 people to Kangju; no border change on the page.
193,930 km2, 14-59. Same land; the page dates only the 3 AD death of the chieftain who fled to Kangju.
194,000 km2, 60-67. Unchanged; page silent for these years.
194,501 km2, 68-77. 'In 74 AD the Wusun are recorded as having sent tribute to the Han military commanders in Cheshi'.
194,000 km2, 78-83. 'In 80 AD Ban Chao requested assistance from the Wusun against the city-state Quchi (Kucha)'.

Unverified: page silent on the year. The shape falls from 194 k to 39.9 k km2 and stays there to 450 (Issyk-Kul only, 75.7-80.1 E). The page says only that 'During the 2nd century AD the Wusun continued their decline in political importance'. The Yueban page has a Xiongnu remnant that 'conquered Zhetysu, where they established the principality of Yueban' (undated; infobox 'Established: 160'), which is the likeliest cause; ledger 91 records the loss at confidence 1.
37,767 km2, 106-153. Unverified: page silent for the 2nd century beyond the decline.
39,947 km2 for 165-386. Unverified: the page has nothing on the 3rd or 4th centuries.
38,933 km2, 387-401. Unverified: page silent; neighbours then were the Xionites (xionites dossier) and the Protectorate row.

38,079 km2, 402-442. 'In the 5th century AD the Wusun were pressured by the Rouran and may have migrated to the Pamir Mountains' (Wusun page); the Rouran page (khaganate from 402, 2.8 M km2 in 405) does not mention the Wusun.

38,079 km2, 443-450. 'They are last mentioned in Chinese historical sources in 436 AD, when a Chinese envoy was sent to their country and the Wusun reciprocated'; 'It is possible that they became subsumed into the later Hephthalites'. The shape runs 14 years past the last mention; kept (ledger 450, confidence 1).

region.text: the Ili Valley and the Issyk-Kul basin: 'the Wusun drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled the area'; the royal court Chigu 'in a side valley leading to Issyk Kul'

ledger.note: 132 BC: the Wusun take the Ili Valley. 'In 133-132 BC, the Wusun drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled the area.' Liejiaomi, the infant son of the king killed around 173 BC, had been adopted by the Xiongnu ruler; the Xiongnu dossier draws the Wusun as its vassal here until about 115 BC.

region.text: the Ili Valley and the Issyk-Kul basin: 'the Wusun drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled the area'; the royal court Chigu 'in a side valley leading to Issyk Kul'

ledger.note: 132 BC: the Yuezhi are driven from the Ili. 'Liejiaomi attacked the Yuezhi in the Ili Valley' (the Yuezhi hold it from about 165 BC, Yuezhi dossier). The page names the valley; the Issyk-Kul side is the researcher's reading of Chigu's 'side valley leading to Issyk Kul'.

region.text: the Ili Valley and the north of the old Wusun land, outside the 91 shape

ledger.note: 91: Wusun land shrinks to Issyk-Kul. Bridged from Cliopatria's shape (194 k to 40 k km2); the Wusun page says only that 'During the 2nd century AD the Wusun continued their decline in political importance', and the Yueban page that a Xiongnu remnant 'conquered Zhetysu, where they established the principality of Yueban' (undated; infobox est. 160). Page silent on the year and the taker.

450: Cliopatria's last Wusun shape ends. The page: 'In the 5th century AD the Wusun were pressured by the Rouran and may have migrated to the Pamir Mountains'; 'last mentioned in Chinese historical sources in 436 AD'; 'possible that they became subsumed into the later Hephthalites'. Page silent on the year of the end; 450 is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Wusun conquest of the Ili Valley

zones.text: the Ili Valley and the Issyk-Kul basin: 'the Wusun drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled the area'; the royal court Chigu 'in a side valley leading to Issyk Kul'

wars.outcome: The Wusun, with Xiongnu support, drove the Yuezhi out of the Ili Valley and settled it.
wars.note: Dated '133-132 BC' on the Wusun page; the Yuezhi page (yuezhi dossier) has 132 BC 'in alliance with the Xiongnu'.

wars.name: Xiongnu attack on the Wusun and the Han-Wusun campaign of 72 BC
wars.outcome: Around 80 BC the Xiongnu inflicted a devastating defeat on the Wusun; in 72 BC 'the joint forces of the Wusun and Han invaded the territory of the Luli King of the Right', and Han and Wusun together broke the Xiongnu.
wars.note: No border moved in the Wusun's own land; the Han-Xiongnu War page also has Wusun, Dingling and Wuhuan raiding the Xiongnu in the following year.

certainty.note: Steppe and mountain valleys: the page gives no frontier line; the neighbours are described only by direction (Kangju to the north-west, Dayuan to the west).

notes: One state, not several: the Wusun page shows one kunmi kingdom from 133-132 BC to its last mention in 436, so the 620-year Cliopatria row is not split. It starts 38 years too early (-170 puts the Wusun on the Ili before they took it) and has no shape for -144..-67; both are corrected (wusun_-170 wrong, wusun_-132 new). The big change is 91, from 194 k to 40 k km2, which no page explains; ledger 91 is confidence 1 and the shape is kept. The 3rd-4th centuries are unverified (page silent). End 450 is Cliopatria's; the page's last mention is 436 and its alternatives are a migration to the Pamirs or absorption by the Hephthalites. Not drawn here (belong to other dossiers or the suzerain's ledger): the Wusun as a Xiongnu vassal 132-c. 115 BC (xiongnu dossier, already there), as a Han ally (Zhang Qian 115 BC; the princesses Xijun 110-105 BC and Jieyou, d. 49 BC) and as a Han tributary from 51 BCE (Protectorate page; the han-dynasty dossier should carry a vassal_start with counterpart wusun), the division into Greater and Lesser Kunmi (Yuanguimi and Wujiutu, undated on the page, after about 64 BC), the 2 BC flight of a chieftain to Kangju. The Wusun's Hexi homeland before 173 BC is not drawn. States that need dossiers: Kangju (neighbour to the north-west), Dayuan (Ferghana; this batch writes great-yuan, the Cliopatria row 'Great Yuan'), Yueban (Zhetysu, est. 160, ended 480s; the xiongnu dossier already lists it). No unknown gazetteer names. Budget: five pages of nine.
